n: The ark is placed in David’s tent in Jerusalem, and the people offer burnt offerings (wholly given to God) and peace offerings (shared in fellowship).

f.g: Offerings completely burned, symbolizing total dedication to God.
Fellowship offerings, partly eaten by the worshippers in a joyful meal.

n: David blesses the people in the Lord’s name, acting as a shepherd-king who points his people to God.

f.w: blessed the people in the name of the LORD

n: He gives every man and woman food for a celebration—bread, meat and a cake of raisins or wine. Everyone shares in the joy.

f.g: Probably a cake of raisins (Hebrew ’ashishah), a festive food.
No one is left out of the celebration.

n: David appoints Levites to serve continually before the ark: to remember, give thanks and praise God. Worship becomes an ongoing, organized part of national life.

f.g: Or “to invoke” or “to remember”—calling God’s deeds to mind in worship.

f.w: to thank and praise the LORD

n: Asaph leads, with other Levites on lyres and harps; Asaph sounds the cymbals.
Two priests blow trumpets regularly before the ark.
David gives Asaph a psalm of thanksgiving. What follows weaves together parts of Psalms 105, 96 and 106.

f.g: Gave this psalm to be sung—the first time thanksgiving was formally assigned to Asaph’s choir.

n: The psalm opens with a call to thank the Lord, pray to Him, and tell others what He has done. Worship naturally leads to witness.

f.w: make known his deeds among the people

n: Sing to Him and talk about His wonderful works. Praise is meant to fill both songs and conversation.

f.w: talk ye of all his wondrous works

n: Take pride in God’s holy name; let those who seek Him be glad.

f.w: Glory ye in his holy name
f.g: Boast in, or delight in, God’s name.

n: Seek the Lord and His strength; seek His face always. Seeking God continually is the heartbeat of the chronicler’s message.
Remember His miracles and the judgments He has spoken. Remembering is a key covenant duty throughout scripture.

f.g: The decisions and laws God has spoken.

n: The psalm addresses Israel as God’s chosen family, descendants of Jacob.

f.g: Descendants of Israel (Jacob). Psalm 105:6 reads “seed of Abraham.”

n: The Lord is Israel’s God, yet His authority reaches all the earth.

f.w: his judgments are in all the earth

n: Always remember His covenant, which He commanded for a thousand generations—that is, forever.

f.w: Be ye mindful always of his covenant

n: This is the covenant God made with Abraham and swore to Isaac—the Abrahamic covenant that Latter-day Saints believe continues through temple and gospel covenants today.

f.w: the covenant which he made with Abraham

n: God confirmed this covenant to Jacob as an everlasting decree.
The covenant included the promise of the land of Canaan as Israel’s inheritance.

f.g: Your allotted portion—as though measured out by a surveyor’s line.

n: God made this promise when the patriarchs were few in number and lived as foreigners in the land.

f.g: Foreigners or resident aliens.

n: They wandered from nation to nation—Canaan, Egypt and beyond.
God protected them and even rebuked kings for their sake, such as Pharaoh and Abimelech in Abraham’s day.

f.w: he reproved kings for their sakes

n: God’s warning to the nations: do not touch My anointed ones or harm My prophets. The patriarchs are called prophets because they received revelation.
The psalm now calls all the earth to sing and announce God’s salvation every day. The message reaches beyond Israel to all peoples.

f.w: Sing unto the LORD, all the earth
shew forth from day to day his salvation

n: Declare His glory among the nations—a missionary vision for God’s people.

f.w: Declare his glory among the heathen

f.g: The nations; non-Israelite peoples.

n: The Lord is great and worthy of praise and reverence above all supposed gods.
The gods of the nations are mere idols, but the Lord created the heavens. Only the Creator deserves worship.

f.w: all the gods of the people are idols
f.g: Hebrew ’elilim—“nothings” or “worthless things.”

n: Glory, honor, strength and joy fill God’s presence.

f.w: strength and gladness are in his place
f.g: Psalm 96:6 reads “strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.”

n: All peoples are invited to give the Lord the glory and strength He deserves.

f.g: Families of the nations.

n: Bring an offering and come worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness.

f.g: Possibly “in holy attire” or “in the splendor of His holiness.”

n: All the earth should stand in awe of Him; He holds the world steady.

f.w: the world also shall be stable

n: Heaven and earth rejoice; let the nations proclaim, “The LORD reigns!”
The sea, the fields and all creation join the celebration. Creation itself is pictured as worshipping its Maker.
The trees sing because the Lord is coming to judge the earth. Christians and Latter-day Saints see this as anticipating Christ’s Second Coming, when He will reign in righteousness.

f.w: he cometh to judge the earth

n: A familiar refrain: give thanks, for the Lord is good and His mercy lasts forever. This line became a standard chorus in Israel’s worship.

f.g: Hebrew hesed—steadfast, covenant love.

n: A prayer for deliverance and gathering from among the nations. To the chronicler’s post-exile readers, scattered among other lands, these words would have felt very personal.
The psalm closes with a blessing to the Lord forever, and all the people respond, “Amen!” and praise Him.

f.w: And all the people said, Amen
f.g: “Amen” means “so be it” or “truly,” affirming what was said.

n: David leaves Asaph and his fellow Levites to serve before the ark daily.

f.g: According to each day’s needs.

n: Obed-edom and sixty-eight relatives serve as well, with Obed-edom and Hosah as gatekeepers.

f.g: Sixty-eight.

n: Meanwhile the old tabernacle of Moses stood at Gibeon, where Zadok and the priests continued serving at its altar. Worship took place at two sites until Solomon built the temple.

f.w: the high place that was at Gibeon

n: The priests at Gibeon offered burnt offerings every morning and evening, as the law of Moses required.
Heman, Jeduthun and other chosen musicians served at Gibeon, giving thanks because the Lord’s mercy endures forever.

f.g: Likely the same as Ethan, the Merarite music leader (1 Chronicles 15:17).

n: They played trumpets, cymbals and instruments set apart for sacred music. Jeduthun’s sons served as gatekeepers.

f.g: Instruments dedicated to sacred worship.

n: The celebration ends; everyone goes home, and David returns to bless his own household.

f.w: David returned to bless his house
